title: First Draft: Is Ayanna Pressley About to Challenge Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker?
author: Martin Pengelly
content:
_**🚨 BIG NEWS:** On Wednesday evening, more than a week after midterm election
day, the Mississippi Senate race was [called](https://www.theguardian.com/us-
news/2026/nov/11/scott-colom-mississippi-senate-race) for Democrat Scott
Colom, defeating incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith. Mississippi has not
elected a Democratic senator since the early 1980s and has not had a Black
senator since Reconstruction. Dems now have 55 seats in the Senate, with
Alaska yet to be called._

Good morning. **Martin** here, delighted to bring you the news you need to
start your day, as the end of the first week of the GOP lame-duck Congress
draws near.

In today's '**First Draft** ,' we'll consider a low-key but potentially
telling development in the process of electing a Democratic House speaker - a
quiet move by Rep. **Ayanna Pressley** of Massachusetts that could presage
progressive problems for Rep.**Hakeem Jeffries** of New York, the minority
leader who seems sure he'll grasp the gavel.

We'll also look at another display of gross arrogance by **Pete Hegseth** ,
the Trump toady defense secretary who followed escaping impeachment thanks to
Democratic incompetence by managing to earn a loud rebuke from one of his own
troops at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. Is there no beginning to his
talents? There's Iran war news too. Let's dive in.

# 'If It Were up to Ayanna Pressley…'

Answering a petition with a petition might not seem like a major step on the
road to great power, but Rep. Ayanna Pressley's move on Wednesday may yet turn
out to be more meaningful than it might now seem.

**" If it were up to Ayanna Pressley,"** the
[petition](https://act.ayannapressley.com/sign/soc-pressley-agenda/) launched
by the Massachusetts progressive began, **" we'd use our Democratic majority
to fight for: Saving health care. Not just reversing Republicans' cuts -
advancing Medicare for ALL. Passing national abortion protections. Not just
restoring what was stripped away - expanding reproductive rights. Stopping
data centers. Putting real guardrails and oversight in place over the AI
industry. Abolishing ICE. Period.**

**" We need to show that an agenda like this has real, public support. Sign
our petition to demonstrate how many people are calling for this."**

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

And there is real public support for Pressley to take a position leading the
new Democratic House - for where the party goes to indeed be** "up to" **her.
Not huge support yet, sure, but noticeable. On Wednesday night, the
[petition](https://www.change.org/p/make-ayanna-pressley-the-speaker-of-the-
house) on Change.org that seemed to have prompted Pressley to launch her own
had 30,000 signatures, and climbing. Its title: "Make Ayanna Pressley the
Speaker of the House."

**" For many Americans,"** the petition [said](https://www.change.org/p/make-
ayanna-pressley-the-speaker-of-the-house), **" Ayanna Pressley represents a
beacon of hope and integrity in a tumultuous political landscape. She is
someone we can trust, whose genuine commitment to justice and equality
resonates deeply with millions of us across the country. This is not just
about politics; it's about believing in someone who champions the core values
of fairness, transparency, and representative democracy that truly reflect the
diverse voices of America."**

The message didn't go there, but the implication was clear: Pressley, 52 and
in Congress since 2019, a high-profile House progressive, can provide the kind
of leadership that Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York, the minority leader and
presumed speaker in waiting, very patently cannot.

So what happens next?
